text: What brings you in here today? I've been feeling breathless and it's getting worse, so I wanted to check it out.
summary: The patient presents with worsening breathlessness.

text: When did you first start feeling breathless? About two months ago. It came on gradually over time.
summary: The breathlessness began two months ago and developed gradually.

text: How often do you feel breathless? It's worse when I walk more than 50 meters. Exertion is the main trigger.
summary: Breathlessness is mainly triggered by exertion, especially walking short distances.

text: Before two months ago, I could walk normally. I sometimes have a cough with frothy sputum.
summary: Previously normal exercise tolerance, now associated with cough and frothy sputum.

text: The breathlessness has been getting worse over the last two months. Lying flat makes it worse and I gasp for air.
summary: Symptoms are progressively worsening and significantly worse when lying flat.

text: It's worse at night when I'm lying down. I get breathless after climbing three to four steps.
summary: The patient experiences worse symptoms at night and with minimal exertion.

text: Stacking pillows helps my breathing. I haven't had chest pain, recent travel, infections, or surgeries.
summary: Breathlessness improves with positional changes and there are no recent triggering events.

text: I feel more fatigued during the day. I've noticed swelling in my legs starting about two months ago.
summary: The patient reports fatigue and bilateral leg swelling beginning around the same time as breathlessness.

text: I have high blood pressure, diabetes, and high cholesterol. I take aspirin, ramipril, and simvastatin.
summary: The patient has multiple cardiovascular risk factors and is on relevant medications.

text: I had a heart attack four years ago and had a stent placed. I haven't had similar symptoms since then.
summary: Significant past history of myocardial infarction treated with stenting.

text: My father died of a heart attack at 60. I work as a cashier and live alone in an apartment.
summary: There is a family history of heart disease, and the patient lives independently.

text: I used to smoke 10 cigarettes a day for 40 years but quit. I don't drink alcohol or use drugs.
summary: The patient is a former long-term smoker with no current substance use.

text: My activity levels have decreased over the last two months. It's affecting my work and daily routine.
summary: Breathlessness has significantly impacted daily activities and work performance.

text: Based on symptoms and history, congestive heart failure is suspected and further investigations are planned.
summary: The clinician suspects congestive heart failure and plans further evaluation and treatment.
